item.text:
**4B.9 Verdict:** yes, mostly through surveillance, platform/content controls, and administrative harassment. I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a nationwide internet shutdown; the pattern is targeted repression, not blackout.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Vietnam: Repeal Harmful Internet Laws | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/11/vietnam-repeal-harmful-internet-laws | HRW says Decree 147 tightens internet control by forcing data storage and identity verification, requiring 24-hour takedowns, enabling content scanning, account suspensions, and administrative punishments. This is strong evidence of digital control and administrative harassment, though it is post-July and therefore weak for Trọng’s personal attribution. | 4B.9, 4B.6 |
| Yes | Vietnam: EU Should Better Address Intensifying Repression | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-03 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/vietnam-eu-should-better-address-intensifying-repression | HRW reports intrusive surveillance of the internet, state control of all media, and prison sentences for online criticism. This is direct evidence that the state used digital monitoring and information control to suppress political freedom while Trọng was still in effective control. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.7 |
| Yes | Vietnam free prominent journalist | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-07 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/07/vietnam-free-prominent-journalist | HRW says journalist Truong Huy San was detained under Article 331 for Facebook criticism. This is direct evidence of administrative/legal harassment aimed at chilling online speech. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.7 |
| Yes | Vietnam arrests two well-known Facebook users over democratic freedom abuse | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-06-08 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/vietnam-arrests-two-well-known-034901151.html | Reuters reports the arrests of Huy Duc and lawyer Tran Dinh Trien over Facebook posts, with home searches and investigation. This is strong evidence of punitive pressure on critics using online platforms. | 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.7 |
| No | Vietnam: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/vietnam/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House says there were no significant intentional disruptions to internet service or mobile networks during the coverage period. That is the clearest evidence on the “no shutdowns” side, even though it also notes past throttling and proposed blocking powers. | 4B.9 |

**Bottom line**
- Strong evidence for surveillance, content control, account/data restrictions, and arrests of online critics.
- Weak or absent evidence for outright internet shutdowns in 2024.
- The post-July Decree 147 evidence is best treated as regime-line / legacy evidence, not as direct personal action by Trọng after July 18, 2024.

**Search gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 reporting of a full internet shutdown or nationwide blackout in Vietnam under Trọng.
- The concrete 2024 record is narrower and more consistent: surveillance, takedown demands, identity/data controls, and arrests for online speech.
